title: The integral Roos pullback realizes the derived limit of its normalized finite derived pair
statement: Fix ell,E,X,Y,g as in [def-pod-integral-completed-comparison-data] and a normalized finite strict-tower comparison C [lem-a1-finite-pullback-strict-tower-comparison]. Define H=derived_Y ⋙ C.B.functor ⋙ Rlim_X, with Rlim the actual total right derived limit on strict towers of completed integral module sheaves. For a complex P in the published completed coefficients, define H's nth computation projection by applying Rlim to C.B's counit after the exact coefficient-restriction computation isomorphism, followed by the actual derived-limit projection and the exact evaluation computation isomorphism. Given shifts c,d satisfying ShiftCoordinates and ShiftDescent, there is a natural isomorphism a:integral→H on the entire derived category, such that a_QP followed by each of these projections is exactly integralProjection(P,hP,n) for every good transported representative P. The isomorphism a commutes with the composite exact-coefficient, retained finite-pair and actual derived-limit shifts, with d on the integral side. No intrinsic-completeness hypothesis is used.

proof.text: The counit of C.B computes the strict finite pullback tower on good representatives. Exact countable products make the normalized strict Roos comparison an isomorphism from its product mapping fibre to the actual total right derived limit. The universal right-derived pair identifies this limit with the existing completedRlim.

Compose the Roos comparison with the inverse of Rlim of the computation counit. All maps are natural. The fully faithful good resolving localization descends the resulting isomorphism, using the actual integral pullback comparison.

The K-injective normalization fixes every limit projection as the first mapping-cocone coordinate followed by the nth product leg. Retain both exact coefficient and evaluation computation factors to obtain the stated representative equation. The normalized Roos shift identity, finite-pair shift descent and given ShiftDescent identify the two descended shifts and prove the CommShift equation.

theorem integralPullback_roosFiniteTower
    (C : FinitePullbackStrictTower.Comparison.{u, u} l E g)
    (c : (integralOperationsPullbackComplexFunctor.{u, u} l E g).CommShift ℤ)
    (hc : ShiftCoordinates l E g c)
    (d : (integralDerivedPullback.{u, u} l E g).CommShift ℤ)
    (hd : ShiftDescent l E g c d) :
    ∃ a : integral l E g ≅ finiteTowerLimit l E g C,
      (∀ (P : CochainComplex
          (pbcModules Y (pbcAdicCompletion Y (pbcIntegralDatum l E))) ℤ)
        (hP : integralOperationsGoodComplex.{u, u} l E Y ((complexes l E Y).obj P))
        (n : ℕ),
        a.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫ finiteTowerLimitProjection l E g C P n =
          integralProjection l E g P hP n) ∧
      (fun [_d : (integralDerivedPullback.{u, u} l E g).CommShift ℤ] ↦
        NatTrans.CommShift a.hom ℤ) (_d := d)
